column1: # The ACTUAL call graph of each ELIGIBLE candidate, in the form
#   production caller -> legacy authority function -> candidate semantic
# The observable compiler result is the point at which the decision
# changes a COMPILED PROGRAM, not merely an internal AST field.
# Schema: candidate_id <TAB> direct_call_sites <TAB> call_site_count <TAB> production_caller_chain <TAB> observable_compiler_result <TAB> delegation_seam

column4: parseExpr (src/prslib.c:1343) -> parseGetPriority -> the precedence value -> next_prec (:1430,:1435) -> the right-recursion depth of the expression parser -> THE SHAPE OF EVERY BINARY AND UNARY EXPRESSION AST in every compiled program; and therefore the operator grouping, the short-circuit structure of && and ||, and the assignment associativity
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct static call, no callback contract, no diagnostic seam, no recovery): the C wrapper stays C-owned and forwards the scalar

column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct static call).  The out-param is a caller stack local, so the ABI is (I64 tk_type,I64 punct) -> (I64 valid,I64 binop)

column4: parseExpr (src/prslib.c:1343) -> astBinOpFromToken -> the AstBinOp -> parseCreateBinaryOp (:1475) -> astBinaryOp -> THE AST OPERATOR AND RESULT TYPE of every binary expression in every compiled program
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct call across a translation unit).  The out-param is a caller stack local

column4: parseExpr (:1391) and parseUnaryExpr (:1698) -> astUnaryOpFromToken -> the AstUnOp -> astUnaryOperator -> THE AST OPERATOR of every unary expression in every compiled program
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct call across a translation unit).  The out-param is a caller stack local

column4: parseCreateBinaryOp (src/prslib.c:1318) -> astBinOpToTokenPunct -> op_tok -> the BINARY-OPERATOR DIAGNOSTIC message (:1440,:1446) -> THE DIAGNOSTIC TEXT of every invalid binary-operator error
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct static call).  The result is diagnostic-only, not an AST field

column4: parsePrintfFormatCheck (src/prslib.c:852) -> parseCountPrintfFormatSpecs -> the expected argument count -> the format/argument-count DIAGNOSTIC (:884,:891) -> WHETHER A PRINTF CALL WITH A MISMATCHED ARGUMENT COUNT IS ACCEPTED OR REJECTED
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct static call).  The input is a byte buffer with an explicit length

column4: parsePrintfFormatCheck (:864) and parseFunctionArguments (:916) -> parseFormatArgIdx -> the format argument index -> WHICH ARGUMENT IS TREATED AS THE FORMAT STRING -> WHETHER A PRINTF-STYLE CALL IS FORMAT-CHECKED AT ALL, AND WHICH ARGUMENT IS CHECKED
column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct static call).  The input is a byte buffer with an explicit length

column5: ORDINARY CALL SITE (a direct call across a translation unit).  NOTE: this decision is observable in TRANSPILER OUTPUT, not in the emitted machine code
